references.observed: 1873–74 Gothic Revival church; three-stage tower and broach spire, corner pinnacles, triple niche, paired two-light belfry openings, arcaded frieze and pierced parapet, two lucarne tiers, five-bay nave with three-light plate tracery.
Simplified 18.25 by 35.55 m outline covers the church AND rear hall. It is not a nave-only footprint. Tower projection and internal roof divisions need photographic interpretation.

Full panorama pixels verified in isolated offscreen Chrome. Sainsbury-facing tower wall has two lower-stage lancets above a quatrefoil round window; paired belfry and triple niche above. Nave flank and slate roof visible.

Car-park view: nave north elevation with alternating three-light tracery, buttresses and closed slate slope. Rear brick hall north gable has three upper windows, two ground windows and red door with stone surround; pale string courses.
Rear car-park view: hall ridge perpendicular to nave, approximately six tall rear sashes, lower connector, plain high church rear gable. Hall dimensions and hidden south face estimated.

Verified aerial: rear hall finishes substantially ahead of Sainsburys back wall, leaving the car-park aisle clear. Approximate clicked roof/corner coordinates establish the hall position; roof parallax and overhang prevent survey precision. Nave/hall subdivision is calibrated inside the combined OSM envelope, not appended beyond it.

uncertainties: All heights and small metric projections are visually calibrated, not surveyed.
Main nave rear gable corroborated plain by car-park imagery; hall south elevation and exact hall footprint remain estimated.
Fine foliage/crockets and plate tracery are interpreted geometry; no claimed scan equivalence.
Name identifies the historic building; 2021 URC signage is not a claim of present occupancy or worship programme.
